July 2012 ## Tightness behind backwardation shifted forward - The global copper market is in deficit, but price direction is still being determined by the impact of developments in the Eurozone saga on investor sentiment. The uncertainty over how Greece would vote and what Eurozone leaders would decide at the latest conference led funds to go short in June. - The acute backwardation on the LME ended in June, but the tightness between dates behind it never fully cleared just shifted forward. Therefore it is possible there will be another squeeze, especially as one warrant holder emerged holding up to 40-50% of LME warrants in June. - Physical demand growth remains subdued across the world. Spot premia have been left to respond to the relative availability of cathode, with premia in the US rising as exchange stocks continue to fall, while in China they have risen from recent lows and in Europe they remain unchanged. |The supply/demand

However, the fundamentals remain firmly in the background, as the copper price on the LME continues to seesaw mainly in response to developments in the on-going Eurozone saga. At the start of June, the end of the short covering rally saw cash prices fall and the cash-to-3m backwardation unwind. The price then tested downside support and found it, with the 3-month price hitting an intra-day traded low of $7,270/t on 8th June. Given the high level of uncertainty, prices then traded sideways ahead of the Greek election on 17th June. The results of the Greek election were as positive as could be expected and the copper price rallied to over $7,600/t on 19th June. However, the internal contradictions of the Eurozone prompted bond markets to turn on Spain and Italy, driving bond yields for their sovereign debt towards the crisis levels of 7%. In response, investors fled back to safe havens and the copper price fell back to test the recent downside support level, which held again. The next turn of the short term price cycle came after the results of the Eurozone summit on 28th June, which boosted sentiment among financial investors. The strict stance of German Chancellor Angela Merkel against bailing out struggling banks was softened. Among the measures taken, the European Stability Mechanism was allowed to directly recapitalise banks with its debt having the same level of seniority as existing loans in the event of bankruptcy. As a result, febrile sentiment switched rapidly into "risk on" mode, with the 3-month price on the LME jumping to a trading high of $7,819/t on 3rd July. ### Still tight in June despite end of acute backwardation LME forward curve, cash=100, Jan 12–Jun 12 The acute backwardation disappeared by early June following the massive exports from China to Asian LME warehouses. However, the tightness between dates behind the move into backwardation never really fully cleared. Instead of moving into a smooth contango structure (with the price for each forward date higher than the previous one) in June the kink in the curve shifted out a few months to the September contract (see chart). The LME warrant banding report also showed that a dominant warrant holder had arrived, with one player holding 4050% of the stocks in LME warehouses in June, but that this fell to 30-40% as of 3rd July. 100.5

They had announced in early June that that they would export cathode to “rebalance” the market. The lag for shipment time for exports to arrive in LME Asian warehouses imply that the 100,000t exported in May is likely to account for most of the metal shipped under this programme. ## Funds go short… On balance, commodity investors sold in the face of Greece’s inability to form a government following its elections in mid-April. The subsequent deterioration in the European banking sector, worries about the sovereign debt burdens of both Spain and Italy, and a slowing European economy, all caused the euro to weaken, providing investors with further incentive to sell commodities. For the same reasons, investor confidence in higher copper prices waned considerably over the last month as well. According to the weekly CFTC Commitments of Traders reports, as of May 22nd , Managed Money traders in the COMEX copper contract had reversed their net long, and were net short by 2,808 contracts. As of June 26th , however, these traders were net short by 13,769 contracts (see the chart to the right), the largest net short position posted since 24th March 2009. Data: CFTC, *weekly to 26th June 2012 ## …and then get caught short All of this changed on 29th June when the EU announced that it would appoint a supranational banking supervisor for the region and allow EU bailout funds to be disbursed directly to lenders, thus bypassing national governments. Investors reacted very favourably to this news, and the LME 3-month copper price rallied by about $350/t following the announcement. On July 2nd , PMI results for June were rather discouraging across the board, but market participants seemed unconcerned. Instead, the LME 3-month copper price continued to rise to the high mentioned above of $7,819/t on the 3rd . Given that there are rumours in the market that the dominant warrant holder is one of the large traders, there may be a repeat of the squeeze

seen in April and May. As they had cleared their positions by delivering so much metal into the LME warehouses, the Chinese smelters are unlikely to be the ones holding the exposed short positions. During the recent decline in prices to this year's lows, there was some short selling on the LME, as evidenced by the price decline being accompanied by a rise in open © 2012 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 3 of 18 Copper Monitor July 2012 www.crugroup.com interest on the LME. So it may be that this time a squeeze could be between a trader and financial investors in the copper market. ## SHFE forward curve also remains in backwardation The Shanghai market forward curve has also been in backwardation, with the Shanghai Metal Market spot metal price above both the SHFE cash month and 3-month prices for most days since 5th May. This was understandable in May given the huge exports that month, which would have required buying of physical copper that raised nearby prices above prices further forward. Domestic cathode production has been sustained while refined consumption growth by the semis industry has not been all that strong. Net imports fell by only 46,000t in May, as record exports were offset to a degree by rising imports. We estimate that refined consumption in China was 692,000t in May, as semi fabricators turned to use more scrap in their raw material mix (see chart). So the monthly supply/demand balance in China was a 32,000t deficit. However, the continuation of the backwardation into June is less easily explained. Consumption growth seems to have been good but not great over the past month, as semis producers face high inventories of both semis and semis containing end use products. For their part, SHFE and bonded stocks fell by a combined 135,000t, so the Chinese market was in deficit again last month. Consumption may have picked up marginally compared to May, but the most likely reason for the deficit and stock drawdown in June is a combination of continued cathode exports throughout H1 June and a decline in cathode imports. This was reflected in the backwardation in the Shanghai market narrowing from an average of RMB334/t for the Shanghai Metal market spot price to the SHFE cash month price in the 1st - 28th June period to an average contango of RMB158/t over the week from 29th June to 5th July. At the same time, the move into a contango market has seen the import premium pick up from an average of around $50/t in May to about $70/t in June, with the

negative SHFE/LME arbitrage falling back from an average of over $250/t in May to about $60/t in June. 

## US and Europe premia diverge on relative availability 

The demand situations in Europe and the USA have diverged over the past month.  Demand remains dire in southern Europe, with some deterioration noted in northern Europe over the past couple of months, as

the summer lull seems to have arrived early following a modest seasonal Q2 upswing.  There are few exchange stocks in the region but, as spot demand is poor, this is only propping up premia at an average of around $80/t, where they have been for the past few months. 

On the other hand, US premia continue to rise, reaching 7.0-8.0¢/lb for delivered metal to an East Coast consumer in June.  US refined consumption growth has been flat year-to-date so far (compared to a 1.9% decline for Western Europe).  However, the main reason for the higher premia in the US is the draining of exchange stocks over the past few months.  US exchange stocks amounted to only 180,000t at the end of June, having fallen by a further 18,000t (month-end to month-end) on top of the 168,000t decline in the first five months of the year.  As the copper price rose over the past week, Comex prices have risen faster than the LME, opening up a positive arb that should see a further drawdown in Comex stocks.  This is due to many of the LME warrants being tightly held and the amount of stock that is available to the market being much less than the headline figures imply. 

## Price should edge higher over the next month 

The negative SHFE/LME arbitrage has widened to an average of almost $200/t in early July, as Chinese buyers fail to follow LME prices higher.  We take the latest cut in interest rates by the Chinese Central Bank as a positive for demand prospects in the world’s largest copper consumer.  While we expect Q3 to see flat y-o-y refined consumption growth, we anticipate that Chinese consumption will pick up in Q4. With the first signs of potentially positive moves by the Eurozone to address the crisis, investor sentiment is likely to return to neutral if not actually move to a positive net exposure in the copper market. 

Technical indicators also support a view that the copper price may have found a floor at the recent lows of just under $7,300/t.  Moving averages (see chart) are starting to turn, as the 30-day average has turned up in early July.  We therefore expect to see copper trade higher on the LME over the next month.  It will have to have support from investors to break through resistance at $7,900/t. However, stock levels in the world ex-China are only equivalent to 2.5 weeks of consumption. Following the very weak Q4 2011, the market for flat rolled copper and copper alloy products registered a partial recovery in Q1 2012. In regional developments, the European market **600** continued to be affected by the uncertain economic prospects, although output and sales recovered partially in Q1. In China, **500** production has increased sharply due to capacity expansions **400** but this has not been matched by consumption. Demand in the US market was relatively robust in Q1, owing to strong **300** downstream demand from producers of connectors. Overall, production of copper flat rolled products reached 507,000t in **200** Q1 2012, an 8% increase q-o-q and a 3% increase compared **100** to the same quarter last year. Production of copper alloy flat rolled products increased by 9% q-o-q and 8% y-o-y, **0** amounting to 560,000t in Q1. On the consumption side, in Q1 both copper and copper alloy PSSF consumption increased by 5% q-o-q reaching 488,000t and 536,000t, respectively. Cu PSSF CuAL PSSF

Overall we estimate that **215** 485,000t of plate, sheet, strip and foil production capacity has **195** been added since the end of Q1 2011.  According to Antaike, **175** there are now more than 300 copper plate, sheet and strip **155** producers in China with a capacity of 3Mt/y, of which **135** 800,000t is high precision copper plate and strip.  However, **115** most of this new production was stockpiled as the market only **95** saw a slight increase in consumption, with both copper and **75** copper alloy increasing by 5%. We understand that copper and copper alloy flat rolled semis fabricators were still under pressure from rising costs and financing difficulties.  This was partly due to the tightening of credit availability by the government in an attempt to reduce inflation, which decreased the net amount of broad credit extended to the economy in Q1.  Another important factor was a general slowdown in downstream demand for copper products stemming from the slowdown in the Chinese economy.  GDP growth in Q1

slowed along with the growth in industrial production to the lowest levels seen in the past 2 years. According to **Antaike** , demand growth in electronics and machinery has been limited and both of these are major end use sectors for copper and copper alloy PSSF.  An important sector-specific development was that the Chinese government ended the old-for-new home appliances scheme in 2011, which gave a 10% discount on selected appliances.  The end of the scheme is likely to have had an effect on sales of appliances which are another major end use sector for copper and copper alloy PSSF.  Beyond the domestic market, Europe’s economic problems may have contributed to a slowdown in downstream demand for copper products in China as well as other Asian markets.  With expanding capacity and lacklustre demand growth, we estimate that the average capacity utilisation rate at flat rolled copper and copper-alloy production facilities was 59% at the end of Q1.  Given the scale of the current production capacity,  the new project launches had a significant diluting effect on utilisation rates, mostly counteracting the weaker than expected growth in demand.  According to Antaike, in the beginning of March producers began reporting higher operating rates in copper strip and plate enterprises.  However, producers were still under pressure as increasing domestic competition from the additional capacity squeezed their profit margins.

Despite registering a 3.4% q-o-q increase in Q1, levels are still 6.2% lower than production in Q2 2011 and further decline is expected in Q2. This is primarily a reflection of a decline in the German auto industry. **Aurubis AG** reported that demand for flat rolled products was higher in the first quarter of this calendar year compared to Q4 2011, although volumes remained below levels observed in Q1 2011. Buyers were reported to be more hesitant and ordering smaller quantities on a shorter notice. Nevertheless, **Aurubis AG** expanded output of flat rolled product and specialty wire by 25% q-o-q to 60,000t in Q1, following the acquisition of Luvata’s Rolled Products Division in September 2011. Looking at the downstream demand in the market, connectors are a major end-use area for copper and copper alloy flat rolled products. **Molex** , a major producer in the industry, reported an overall increase in orders of 7% q-o-q in Q1 2012. However, the y-o-y growth rate was negative at -1%. Key flat rolled end-use segments performed well. Automotive orders were was up 16% q-o-q, Industrial orders increased by 12%, Infotech orders increased by 10% and Consumer Electric orders grew by 1%. However, y-o-y growth rates were much lower and even negative in some sectors. This corresponds to the overall picture for the flat rolled market, with downstream demand lagging behind the previous year. **Amophenol** , another major producer of connectors reported that sales grew by 4% y-o-y and 3% q-o-q, remarking that the automotive, commercial aerospace, broadband communications and industrial markets performed well and offset declines in defence and wireless markets. The general market sentiment is that an upswing in the market is unlikely in the first half of 2012, with both **Aurubis** and the **KME group** indicating that the weakness in the Asian and European markets is likely to continue. **Antaike** expects slow demand growth in China in major copper and copper alloy PSSF end-use sectors, including electronics and machinery. ## Mine Production 



- **Codelco** and **Anglo American** have opted to extend their out-of-court negotiations over Codelco’s contested option to purchase 49% of **Anglo American Sur** until 17<sup>th</sup> July 2012.  Both companies agreed to suspend legal proceedings in late May 2012 in the hope of reaching an outof-court agreement by 22<sup>nd</sup> June 2012.  However, this initial negotiation time frame proved too brief and has been extended. If an agreement is not reached by 17<sup>th</sup> July, the companies will return to the **Civil Court of Santiago** to resolve the dispute. Experts believe that if this is the case, litigation proceedings may last many years. 



- The proposed merger between **Glencore** and **Xstrata** has suffered a major setback after the second-largest shareholder in Xstrata, **Qatar** , withdrew its support for the current deal, demanding improved terms on 27<sup>th</sup> June.  This move came late in the day; a shareholder vote on the deal was scheduled for 12<sup>th</sup> July, but has now been pushed back.  Qatar is demanding 3.25 Glencore shares for every Xstrata share as opposed to the current offer of 2.8 shares. Cumulatively, Qatar and other minority Xstrata shareholders have the power to block the merger.  Following this development, ot

her wavering Xstrata investors have also voiced concerns over the deal, especially due to the hefty compensation packages that have been offered to retain Xstrata executives.  Glencore is already considering changes in the management’s paypackages, but there has been no news of revisions to the share offer. 



- It was announced on 26<sup>th</sup> June that **Barrick Gold** has lost its court case against **Goldcorp** over the right to acquire a stake in **Xstrata** ’s **El Morro project** .  Barrick’s 2009 deal with Xstrata to acquire a 70% stake in the project foundered when minority shareholder **New Gold** exercised its right of first refusal (using money lent by Goldcorp) and subsequently transferred its stake to Goldcorp in January 2010.  Currently expected to be commissioned in 2017, El Morro is set to produce 170,000t/y of copper-in-concentrate at full capacity.

The new regulations will help to differentiate between

## Exploration and Development 



- **Discovery Metals** announced on 28<sup>th</sup> June that it has begun production of copper-silver concentrate at its **Boseto** copper project in Botswana.  The first 500t of concentrate produced had a copper grade of 32%. The concentrator is being fed by the nearby **Zeta** deposit where mining operations have already commenced.  Although the mine has started as an open pit operation, it is set to switch to underground mining by the end of next year.  Subsequently, the company also plans to start mining the **Plutus** deposit.  The Boseto operation has an expected lifespan of at least 5 years and is initially expected to produce 1.1Moz/y of silver and 36,000t/y of copper-inconcent

rate.  The company plans to increase copper production to 50,000t/y by 2016. 



- It was reported on 21<sup>st</sup> June that **Xstrata** had announced plans to sell all or part of its 81.8% stake in the **Frieda River** copper project in Papua New Guinea.  Market insiders estimate the value of Xstrata’s stake in the project at around US$2.2B. The total development cost of the project is estimated to be approximately US$5.3B. Upon commissioning, Frieda River is expected to produce 190,000t/y of copper-in-concentrate. 



- A similar announcement was made by **Lumina Copper** on 15<sup>th</sup> June, with the company considering the full or partial sale of its **Taca Taca** project in Argentina. The Taca Taca project is scheduled to come on stream in 2017, boasting a production capacity of 90,000t/y of copper-in-concentrate.  The project’s development cost is estimated at around US$3.0B.
